source: NERC 2026 Summer Reliability Assessment — Demand and Resource Tables (pp. 45–55) and Key Findings (pp. 1–3)
note: Anticipated Reserve Margin and Reference Margin Level are the 2026 SRA columns of each assessment area's Demand, Resource, and Reserve Margins table. riskSeasonal reflects NERC's Key Findings: all areas assessed adequate for normal summer peak conditions; areas listed as facing elevated risk under more extreme conditions are marked 'elevated'. No resource shortfalls (ARM below RML) are reported in the 2026 SRA.

MRO-SaskPower.riskNote: NERC Key Findings: elevated risk — margins tightened year-on-year; extreme conditions may require maintenance rescheduling, transfers, or demand response.

NPCC-New England.riskNote: NERC Key Findings: elevated risk under extreme summer conditions — anticipated margin just above the reference level and firm imports reduced from the prior year.

Texas RE-ERCOT.riskNote: NERC Key Findings: normal risk area-wide; localized transmission constraints noted for Far West Texas under high demand with low wind/solar output.

WECC-Northwest.riskNote: NERC Key Findings: elevated risk under extreme conditions — drought and early snowmelt affecting a supply fleet that is majority hydropower.
